toc.title: MCP Servers in Claude Code and Agent Workflows (Task 2.4)

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol; URL: uniform resource locator; API: application programming interface

  • Why too many tools hurt, and how to scope tools to roles
  • The three tool_choice modes: auto, any, and forced selection
  • MCP server scoping: project .mcp.json versus user ~/.claude.json, environment variable expansion, resources
  • Choosing among Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob

2Distributing Tools Across Agents (Task 2.3)

Running case

Birchwood Supply's Synthesis Agent Wanders

  • The research system gave every subagent all 18 tools
  • The synthesis agent started running web searches itself, and tool choices became unreliable
  • Meanwhile about four in five of its "verification" needs are simple fact checks (a date, a name)
  • Too many tools (18 instead of 4 or 5) increases decision complexity and degrades selection reliability.
  • Agents given tools outside their specialization misuse them (a synthesis agent trying web searches).
  • Scoped tool access (least privilege): each agent gets only the tools its role needs, plus a few narrow cross-role tools for frequent needs.
  • Replace generic tools with constrained ones: fetch_url → load_document, which validates that the URL is a document URL.
  • Scoped cross-role tool: give the synthesis agent a small verify_fact tool for the common simple checks, and route complex verification through the coordinator to the web search agent.

Exam tip

"Reduce round-trips but keep reliability" → a scoped tool for the common case (least privilege), with the coordinator still handling the rare complex case. Giving all web-search tools to the synthesis agent over-provisions it.

tool_choice

Setting Behavior Use it when
"auto" (default with tools) The model may call a tool or answer in text Normal agent behavior
"any" The model must call a tool, but picks which You need structured output and several schemas fit; the document type is unknown
Forced: {"type": "tool", "name": "..."} The model must call that named tool A specific step must run first, e.g. extract_metadata before enrichment tools; then handle later steps in follow-up turns

[Verify live] In current API documentation, forced tool use (any and tool) returns an error on some models: it is not supported with manual extended thinking, and it returns a 400 error on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1. The documented alternatives are auto with strict tool use (schema-valid inputs) or structured outputs (output_config.format). The exam guide still teaches "any" and forced selection, so answer as the guide teaches; in real code, check the model's support first. As of 8 November 2026.

3MCP Servers in Claude Code and Agent Workflows (Task 2.4)

Question Answer
Where do shared team servers go? Project scope: .mcp.json in the repository, shared through version control
Where do personal or experimental servers go? User scope: ~/.claude.json, not shared
How to keep tokens out of the repo? Environment variable expansion in .mcp.json, e.g. ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
Are all servers' tools available together? Yes: tools from all configured servers are discovered at connection time and available simultaneously
How to reduce exploratory calls? Expose content catalogs as MCP resources (issue summaries, documentation hierarchy, database schemas)
Build or reuse? Use an existing community server for standard integrations (e.g. Jira); build a custom server only for team-specific workflows
Agent prefers built-in Grep over a better MCP tool? Enhance the MCP tool's description to explain capabilities and outputs in detail 
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "issues": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/issues",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${ISSUES_TOKEN}" }
    }
  }
}

[Verify live] Current Claude Code documentation names three scopes: local (default, stored in ~/.claude.json, private to you in one project), project (.mcp.json, shared) and user (all your projects). When a name appears in several, local beats project beats user. Project servers need your approval in interactive use. Expansion supports ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default}. MCP tools appear as mcp__<server>__<tool>, and newer versions can defer loading MCP tool definitions until needed. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Shared team servers go in the project .mcp.json with ${ENV_VAR} tokens; personal or experimental servers go in the user ~/.claude.json.

4Built-in Tools (Task 2.5)

Tool Use it to... Remember
Grep Search file contents (function names, error messages, imports) First step to find entry points and callers
Glob Find files by name pattern (**/*.test.tsx) Path patterns, not contents
Read Load a whole file To follow imports and trace flow
Write Create or fully rewrite a file Replaces the content
Edit Targeted change by matching unique text Fails if the text is not unique
Bash Run shell commands (tests, git) Use for execution, not for searching code

  • When Edit fails because the anchor text appears more than once: Read the file, then Write the corrected full file (the reliable fallback).
  • Build understanding incrementally: Grep for entry points, Read to follow imports and trace flows, rather than reading every file up front.
  • Trace usage through wrapper modules: first list the exported names, then Grep each name across the codebase.
Exam tip

Edit needs unique anchor text; when it is not unique, Read then Write. Search content with Grep and find names with Glob.

5Exam Q&A

S1Birchwood's synthesis agent has all 18 tools, keeps performing its own web searches, and picks wrong tools. What is the best change?

  • AAsk it nicely in the prompt to avoid web searches
  • BRemove the coordinator
  • CGive it even more tools, including every search tool, so that it never needs the coordinator or search agent
  • DRestrict it to a small tool set for synthesis, such as a scoped verify_fact tool, and leave searching to the search agent
Show the answer

Answer: D. Fewer, role-specific tools improve selection and prevent cross-specialization misuse.

S2About four in five of the synthesis agent's verification needs are quick lookups (a date, a name, a figure); the rest need real research. Each round trip through the coordinator adds delay. Which approach is best?

  • AMake it batch all verification needs and return them to the coordinator in one list at the end of its pass
  • BGive it a scoped verify_fact tool for simple lookups and keep complex cases routed through the coordinator
  • CCache extra context around each source in advance
  • DGive it every web search tool
Show the answer

Answer: B. A narrow tool covers the common case; the rest keeps the existing coordination. Full tool access over-provisions the agent, batching creates blocking dependencies and speculative caching cannot predict needs.

S3A pipeline must always run extract_metadata before any enrichment tool. Which setting makes the model call that tool first?

  • Atool_choice: "auto" with a polite reminder in the system prompt to call it first
  • BRemoving extract_metadata from the tool list so that no enrichment tool runs first
  • CForce extract_metadata first, then handle later steps in follow-up turns
  • DSetting max_tokens to 1
Show the answer

Answer: C. Forced selection guarantees the named tool is called; subsequent steps continue in later turns.

S4A document extraction service receives invoices, receipts or contracts and has one extraction schema per type. The type is unknown up front, and the model sometimes replies in plain text. Which tool_choice is best?

  • AForced selection of the invoice tool for every incoming document
  • B"auto"
  • C"any", so the model must call one of the extraction tools
  • DNo tools at all, and parse the model's text reply with a regular expression
Show the answer

Answer: C. "any" guarantees a tool call while letting the model pick the matching schema.

S5Where should a team-shared Jira MCP server be configured, with its token kept out of version control?

  • AIn project-level .mcp.json using ${JIRA_TOKEN} expansion
  • BIn ~/.claude.json on one developer's laptop, with the token written into the file
  • CHard-coded in CLAUDE.md
  • DIn a public README
Show the answer

Answer: A. Project scope shares the server through version control; environment variable expansion keeps secrets out of the file.

S6A developer wants to try a new experimental MCP server without affecting teammates. Where should it go?

  • AProject-level .mcp.json
  • BUser-level configuration (~/.claude.json)
  • CThe shared repository's CLAUDE.md, committed so that the whole team gets the server
  • DA pull request to the main branch so that the whole team reviews the server
Show the answer

Answer: B. Personal and experimental servers belong in user scope; project scope would add it for everyone.

S7A custom MCP search tool is far more capable than Grep, but the agent keeps using built-in Grep. What helps most?

  • ARename the server so that its name sorts ahead of the built-in tools in the list
  • BWrite a detailed description of the tool's capabilities and outputs
  • CAdd more built-in tools
  • DRemove Grep from the system
Show the answer

Answer: B. Better descriptions guide selection toward the more capable tool.

S8Agents repeatedly make exploratory calls to learn which documentation pages exist. Which MCP feature reduces this?

  • ADisabling all resources
  • BExposing the documentation hierarchy as an MCP resource
  • CUsing a longer system prompt that lists every documentation page by hand
  • DAdding more write tools
Show the answer

Answer: B. Resources expose content catalogs so the agent can see what is available without exploratory calls.

S9An Edit call fails because the target text appears in six places. What is the most reliable approach?

  • ADelete the file
  • BRead the file and Write the corrected full contents
  • CRetry the same Edit several times until the text happens to be unique
  • DUse Glob to find the text
Show the answer

Answer: B. When there is no unique anchor, Read plus Write is the dependable fallback.

S10An engineer must find every caller of calculateTotal in an unfamiliar repository. Which first step is best?

  • AGlob for *.total
  • BRead every file in the repository first, then search through what was read
  • CGrep for calculateTotal, then Read the matches to follow the flow
  • DUse Bash to print all files
Show the answer

Answer: C. Grep finds entry points by content; Read then follows imports. Reading everything up front wastes context.

S11Which TWO statements about MCP configuration in Claude Code are correct? Select TWO.

  • AOnly one server's tools are available at a time
  • BEnvironment variable expansion keeps tokens out of the committed file
  • CUser-level ~/.claude.json is shared with teammates automatically
  • DProject-level .mcp.json is shared with the team through version control
  • ETokens must be hard-coded in .mcp.json
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. The project file is shared and can reference ${ENV_VAR} values, so secrets stay out of version control. User scope is personal, and tools from all configured servers are available together.

S12Which TWO statements about tool_choice are correct? Select TWO.

  • AA forced selection makes the model call the named tool
  • Bany makes the model call some tool
  • Cauto never allows a text answer
  • Dany forces one particular tool
  • Eauto always forces a tool call
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. any guarantees a tool call but lets the model choose, and a forced selection names the tool. auto allows either a tool call or text.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Tool count 4 to 5 relevant tools beat 18; too many degrade selection
Scoping Role-specific tools; narrow cross-role tool (verify_fact); constrained replacement (load_document for fetch_url)
tool_choice auto (text or tool) · any (must call some tool) · forced {"type":"tool","name":...} (must call that tool)
MCP scopes Project .mcp.json (shared) · user ~/.claude.json (personal) · ${ENV_VAR} expansion
MCP behavior All servers' tools available at once; resources expose catalogs; prefer community servers; enrich tool descriptions
Grep / Glob Grep = contents; Glob = file names/paths
Read / Write / Edit Read whole · Write replaces · Edit needs unique text; Edit fails → Read + Write
Exploration Grep entry points → Read to follow imports; for wrappers list exports then grep each name
